History: Phrygia had been an ancient kingdom famed in legend for King Midas; by New Testament times it was part of the Roman province of Asia. Phrygians are named among the hearers at Pentecost, and Paul crossed Phrygia on his journeys.
Culture: Phrygian speech and the old mother-goddess cults were giving way to Greek language and Roman ways.
Religion: The mother-goddess cult before conversion; Christian communities grew along Paul's routes.
BibleConnection: Named among the Pentecost hearers; Paul passed through Phrygia and Galatia on his second journey and through Galatia and Phrygia on his third.
